content.question: What is the fastest way to add a second TextView with similar properties to the first one in XML?

options.text: Use Ctrl-C/Cmd-C to copy and Ctrl-V/Cmd-V to paste

content.explanation: As shown in the episode, you can simply copy the previous tag and paste it after the closing bracket to avoid repetitive typing.

content.question: Where exactly should you paste a copied XML tag to ensure it is independent of the previous one?

options.text: Directly after the previous tag has closed
At the very top of the file

content.explanation: You should shift to a new line and paste the tag after the previous one's closing bracket (/> or </Tag>).

content.question: What indicator does Android Studio use to show 'ignorable' or non-critical configuration issues?
content.explanation: Squiggly lines often appear for internal configurations that aren't major errors; the instructor advises ignoring them if the 'bulb' shows no major issues.

content.question: If the suggestion bulb shows 'nothing special' when clicked, what does the instructor recommend for now?
content.explanation: Minor internal configuration warnings that don't prevent the app from building can usually be ignored for simple exercises.

content.question: What is the primary purpose of clicking the 'Play' button in Android Studio?

options.text: To build and run the app on the emulator

content.explanation: The play button initiates the build process and launches the app specifically on a connected emulator or device.

content.question: If you delete mandatory attributes and try to run the app, what behavior will the emulator show?

options.text: The app will display 'Error' in text

content.explanation: Deleting attributes like width and height causes the app to crash because the system doesn't know how to render the elements.

content.question: Review: Which keyboard layout was recommended for Windows users in Section 1?
content.explanation: Section 1 mentioned that US International is standard for most development environments to avoid character confusion.

content.question: True or False: Every XML tag must have a closing statement or be self-closing.
content.explanation: XML syntax strictly requires every opening tag to be closed either via /> or a separate </Tag>.

content.question: What does the 'build' process do in Android Studio?

options.text: Compiles code and resources into an executable app

content.explanation: The build process takes your source code (XML/Kotlin) and prepares it to run on a device.

content.question: If you are on a Mac, which keys replace 'Ctrl-C' and 'Ctrl-V'?
content.explanation: On macOS, the Command key is used for global shortcuts instead of Control.

content.question: The 'Ctrl-C' action is known as ______ and 'Ctrl-V' is known as ______.
content.explanation: These are the standard shortcut identifiers for Copying and Pasting content.

content.question: Why would an XML tag show a squiggly line if it's identical to the one above it?

options.text: Due to missing IDs or overlapping layout concerns

content.explanation: Even though tags can be copied, they often need unique IDs or layout constraints to distinguish them from each other in the UI hierarchy.

content.question: Review: In Section 1, what was the first and most important step to do before installing Android Studio?
content.explanation: Section 1 emphasized that checking if your PC or Mac meets the RAM and CPU requirements is crucial before installation.

content.question: How do you 'Reload' or 'Rerun' the app on the emulator quickly?

options.text: Click the Play button or the 'Rerun' icon

content.explanation: You can use the Play button to rebuild and rerun the app to see recent changes.

content.question: Which view mode in Android Studio was used in Episode 4 to see the XML code?
content.explanation: Code View is necessary to manually edit XML tags, copy, and paste them as shown in the video.
